title: Raleigh puts data centers on pause while it rewrites the rules
source_used: WRAL (Axios page returned only a security block; text from WORKDIR/fulltext/C09-15.txt was a Cloudflare notice)
key_facts: Raleigh City Council voted 7-1 on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026 for a six-month pause on developing new, larger data centers.
The draft sets 60 days for research and rule drafting, then 120 days for the changes to go through the legislative process.
Advocates wanted 32 months; Mary Black of the Raleigh Anti-Data Center Coalition says six months leaves too little time for residents' input.
Apex approved a 12-month pause in April and Cary an 18-month pause in August.
The draft cites electricity and water demand, noise, light pollution and heat islands, and says Raleigh lacks standards for larger data centers.
WRAL says the mayor and council members had not answered its questions on why six months was chosen.
quote_evidence: The measure passed in a 7-1 vote, with councilmember Christina Jones voting against the moratorium.
Raleigh’s draft sets aside 60 days for research and drafting rules, followed by 120 days to move proposed changes through the legislative process.
The moratorium is shorter than the 12-month pause Apex approved in April and the 18-month pause Cary adopted in August.
why_it_matters_hint: Another North Carolina city is pausing larger data centers while it writes rules.
notes: Axios (pool link) returned a Cloudflare block; read WRAL instead. CBS17, ABC11 and the News & Observer headlines on Google News confirm the vote.
